title: CI, OIDC & Reviewed Releases
subtitle: Turn the local quality gate into a pipeline, publish immutable images, and keep infrastructure changes reviewable.
analogy: CI is a repeatable inspection station. OIDC is a short-lived admission ticket for that station, scoped to the right repository/environment. A published package still needs a reviewed deployment decision.
objectives: Run locked dependency installation, linting, formatting and tests in CI.
Explain OIDC trust, audience and subject without long-lived AWS keys.
Publish a SHA-tagged image with narrowly scoped ECR permissions.
Use a reviewed Terraform plan for promotion and rollback.
prerequisites: The Chapter 8 stack and ECR repository exist.
A GitHub repository with main and a production environment; set environment protection rules if your plan supports them.
Keep the same state backend and release.auto.tfvars inputs from Chapter 8.

lessons.title: Separate validation, publication and deployment
body: Pull requests run lint and tests without AWS credentials. Only a push to main may run the environment-protected publisher job. It pushes one immutable image; it does not silently apply infrastructure.

In this learning workflow, CD is a reviewed promotion step using the published SHA in Terraform. A fully automated Terraform deployment needs a protected state backend, serialized applies, separate plan/apply authorization and broader explicitly designed infrastructure permissions; do not reuse the ECR-only role for that.

lessons.title: Trust and permission are two separate policies
body: The OIDC trust policy determines which GitHub identity may assume the publisher role. Its permission policy allows token retrieval and upload only to this ECR repository. The role has no ECS deployment, Terraform or iam:PassRole permissions because this workflow does not perform those operations.

Use exact aud=sts.amazonaws.com and an exact approved sub. For older repositories a protected environment subject may resemble repo:OWNER/REPO:environment:production. GitHub repositories created after July 15, 2026, or opted into immutable subjects, include immutable owner/repository IDs. Match the format your repository actually uses; do not copy a guessed legacy subject or use repo:*.

lessons.title: Pin inputs and preserve ownership
body: The workflow installs a pinned uv release and runs uv sync --locked against the committed lockfile. Container builds use the same lock and a pinned uv image release. For production, review updates and pin third-party Actions and base images to immutable commit/digest references.

The workflow builds committed GitHub source and tags the image with github.sha. Rerunning a publish for a SHA that is already in an immutable ECR repository may be rejected; reuse the existing artifact or commit a new change instead of overwriting the release.

lessons.title: A safe release and rollback are explicit
body: Use the published SHA as image_tag, preserve all other Terraform inputs, and review a saved plan. Terraform creates new task-definition revisions and updates the services. Verify readiness and a complete job after the rollout.

Rollback means selecting a previously verified image SHA and reviewing another plan. An application rollback does not automatically reverse a database migration; design backward-compatible schemas and keep restore procedures separate.

handHoldingSteps: Read GitHub’s current AWS OIDC reference and determine the exact production-environment subject for your repository. Add github_oidc_subject to the existing ignored release.auto.tfvars file without deleting its other settings.

Copy infra/07-oidc.tf into the existing module and plan/apply with your authenticated local operator identity. If your AWS account already has a GitHub OIDC provider, import/reference that existing provider instead of creating a duplicate URL.

Create repository/environment variables AWS_PUBLISH_ROLE_ARN from publisher_role_arn and ECR_URL from ecr_url. The publish job references the production environment; its trust subject must match that environment and your repository’s subject format.
Copy the workflow into .github/workflows/publish.yml, commit the backend and lockfile, then open a pull request. Confirm the quality job runs without AWS access.

Merge to main after review. Approve the protected publishing environment if configured. After publication, edit only image_tag in release.auto.tfvars, review a release plan locally, apply it, and verify a completed job.
concepts: OIDC: A short-lived federated identity replaces a stored AWS access key, but trust-policy scoping still determines who gets access.
Least privilege: ECR publication and infrastructure administration are different permissions and identities.
Release ownership: This workflow publishes; Terraform owns service configuration and task-definition promotion.

commands.command:
uv run --locked ruff check .
uv run --locked ruff format --check .
uv run --locked pytest
git add app tests Dockerfile compose.yaml pyproject.toml uv.lock .github/workflows/publish.yml
git diff --cached
git commit -m "Add tested backend and publishing workflow"
git push -u origin feature/backend-api
commands.explanation: Run exactly the quality checks CI will run, then open a pull request from your feature branch.
commands.expected: The pull request has a green quality job and no AWS publishing job.

commands.command:
terraform -chdir=infra plan -out=identity.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra apply identity.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra output -raw publisher_role_arn
terraform -chdir=infra output -raw ecr_url
commands.explanation: Run after adding the exact OIDC subject input and identity file. Copy these non-secret outputs into GitHub variables.
commands.expected: A publisher role with ECR-only permissions.

commands.command:
# Edit only image_tag in release.auto.tfvars to the SHA published by CI.
terraform -chdir=infra plan -out=release.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra show release.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra apply release.tfplan
commands.explanation: Preserve enable_services, worker_on_ec2 and github_oidc_subject. A code release may also include infrastructure changes; inspect the entire plan.
commands.expected: New task-definition revisions reference the approved SHA.

commands.command:
aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster bootcamp-iac-cluster --services bootcamp-iac-api bootcamp-iac-worker
BASE_URL=$(terraform -chdir=infra output -raw alb_url)
curl --fail "$BASE_URL/ready"
commands.explanation: Use worker-ec2 if that is your selected mode, then repeat the enqueue/jobs verification from Chapter 8.
commands.expected: The rollout stabilizes and the application works end to end.

codeFiles.description: A tightly scoped identity for publishing images. Add to the existing module in this chapter.

walkthrough.title: github_oidc_subject
walkthrough.explanation: A required exact subject input avoids silently trusting a wildcard repository. Determine the actual subject format from GitHub’s current guidance.

walkthrough.title: Federated trust
walkthrough.explanation: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity is restricted to the GitHub provider, AWS audience and approved subject.

walkthrough.title: Publisher permissions
walkthrough.explanation: GetAuthorizationToken requires Resource=*. Upload actions are scoped to one ECR ARN; this does not authorize infrastructure deployment.

codeFiles.code:
name: Test and publish
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  quality:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          version: "0.13.6"
          enable-cache: true
      - run: uv sync --locked --python 3.13
      - run: uv run --locked ruff check .
      - run: uv run --locked ruff format --check .
      - run: uv run --locked pytest
  publish:
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    needs: quality
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    env:
      AWS_REGION: us-east-1
      ECR_URL: ${{ vars.ECR_URL }}
      IMAGE_TAG: ${{ github.sha }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v5
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_PUBLISH_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
      - name: Build and publish immutable image
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          REGISTRY="${ECR_URL%%/*}"
          aws ecr get-login-password --region "$AWS_REGION" |
            docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "$REGISTRY"
          docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t "$ECR_URL:$IMAGE_TAG" .
          docker push "$ECR_URL:$IMAGE_TAG"
          echo "Published $ECR_URL:$IMAGE_TAG" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "Next: review a Terraform plan using image_tag=$IMAGE_TAG." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
codeFiles.description: Quality checks on pull requests; an environment-protected ECR publisher on main.

walkthrough.title: quality
walkthrough.explanation: uv installs the locked Python environment. Ruff and pytest must pass before publication.

walkthrough.title: permissions
walkthrough.explanation: The default is read-only source access; only the publish job can request an OIDC token.

walkthrough.title: Image and promotion
walkthrough.explanation: Build from the repository root and tag github.sha. The summary hands off to a reviewed Terraform promotion, rather than assuming AdministratorAccess in CI.

breakItDrill.title: Reject the wrong subject
breakItDrill.scenario: Configure a deliberately incorrect github_oidc_subject in the isolated lab and attempt publication.
breakItDrill.symptom: The AWS role assumption fails before image upload; widening ECR permissions would not fix the trust failure.
breakItDrill.fix: Restore the exact approved subject and verify environment/repository identity. Never fix it by changing the subject to a broad wildcard.

assignment.title: Write a release record
assignment.description: Record the source SHA, image digest, reviewed plan, migration compatibility assessment, verification job ID, and known-good rollback SHA. Explain which identity performs each step.
assignment.completionHint: Verify the result yourself, then complete the chapter checklist.

recallNote.keyTakeaway: An authenticated pipeline still needs narrowly scoped trust and permissions; publishing and deploying are different actions.
bullets: No static AWS keys in GitHub secrets.
Exact subject and audience belong in the role trust policy.
The publisher role cannot deploy infrastructure.
Preserve release inputs across plan/apply and rollback.
